leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight round-1 files prefer a single-part prize to Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock. Shared: the two-name credit, independent reproduction, and the view that the magic-wavelength scheme and the 1e-18 level are the core. Not shared: citation wording (Johansson, Kroll and Pearce's text refers to the 1e-18 level or precision; Olsson's to magic-wavelength trapping; Lindroth's and Pearce's are plain; Danielsson wants the wording to rest on what the precision has shown, such as redshift tests and many-body clock physics). Supporters also differ on how serious the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is, and on whether the redefinition of the second should come first. Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce state that they moved to B027 after reading the openings, so its breadth is partly a product of round-1 movement.

Two files prefer a single-part prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp for the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators. Shared: the theory-plus-experiment arc, reproduction over about two decades, and the view that it is mature. Both supporters also state the main objections themselves: the credit gap for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased) and the three-dimensional work, and the possible overlap with the 2016 topology prize. Mehlig moved to B057 from B008 after reading the openings; Eriksson holds it as first choice while acknowledging that its support is broad but shallow, and both list B027 among their alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 files prefer a single-part prize with one ballot ID; no member proposes a two-part configuration.
All eight round-1 files name B027 or B057 as the preferred part, and B027 is an alternative for Eriksson and Mehlig, so the committee's discussion is mostly between these two entries.
Every member who addresses B027 accepts that the lattice clock reached about 1e-18 and has been reproduced by independent laboratories; no member disputes the experimental claim.
Every member who addresses B057 accepts that the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators are verified and mature, and that the credit is where the difficulty lies.

Several members who do not prefer them (Danielsson on B040, B036 and B060, Danielsson and Kroll on B032) treat the Higgs entry, circuit QED, trapped-ion logic and atom interferometry as unlikely to be resolved this year, for reasons of credit, closeness to recent prizes or contested precision.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a new invention (the magic-wavelength scheme, many-body clock physics) or an application of the frequency-comb work honoured in 2005 and the ion-control work honoured in 2012. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each flag this; Johansson calls it the deciding issue.

Whether a measurement capability and an instrument, with fundamental results so far in the form of tighter bounds and redshift tests over millimetres, answers a question about nature. Danielsson makes this point against B053 and notes it about B027; Lindroth says the discovery content is a capability rather than a surprise.

Whether aberration-corrected electron microscopy (B053, an alternative for Olsson and Pearce) is physics content for the Physics prize or a tool whose results lie mostly in materials science (Danielsson).

Whether a second topology prize after 2016 adds enough: the committee must say what Z2 band topology in real materials adds beyond topological phases and phase transitions (raised by Eriksson, Mehlig and Danielsson).
attribution_disputes: B027: the credited pair is Katori and Ye. Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Oates and Derevianko are named as outside the credit by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson; Olsson asks whether Ye is the originator or the developer of Katori's concept; Pearce says a third contributor, for example from the other clock groups, could be argued for.

B057: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp leave out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (who predicted the HgTe realisation Molenkamp measured; Zhang is deceased) and the three-dimensional contributors (Fu, Kane and Mele; Moore and Balents; Hasan). Eriksson, Mehlig and Danielsson all name this; Johansson and Lindroth say they cannot judge it.
B053: Krivanek's corrected-STEM work is outside Rose, Haider and Urban (Olsson, Kroll).
B040 (Higgs): Danielsson says three names from two collaborations of thousands would be arbitrary and that 2013 already recognised the discovery.
maturity_disputes: B027: the SI second has not yet been redefined. Olsson, Kroll, Johansson and Pearce treat it as a timing question; Danielsson treats it as supporting the timing; Kroll and Pearce ask whether to wait for it.

B036 and B060: Danielsson argues that the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits (B036) and the 2012 prize for trapped-ion control (B060) make these a poor fit now, whereas Johansson regards circuit QED as mature and as complementing the 2025 prize.
B057: Eriksson describes the field as mature and arguably overdue, but also reads the opening ballots as broad but shallow (seven ranked, two top-three), whereas B027 has five top-three placements.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works on superconducting circuit QED at Chalmers; he flags a clear connection to B036 and some to B060, and says he should recuse or weigh his vote with care on B036. Neither is in his preferred configuration.

Kroll is on the executive team of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, linked to Chalmers and Johansson; he asks that his B036 ranking be read with that in mind. His work on rare-earth quantum memories overlaps loosely with B060 and B036.

Olsson states that spherical-aberration correction (B053) is her own field (transmission electron microscopy), she is IFSM president, and her community overlaps with the corrector developers; she lists no co-authorship with Rose, Haider or Urban and suggests the committee consider this if B053 advances. She also notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague who works on circuit QED.
Lindroth is an atomic theorist and a long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate); she says this does not involve Katori or Ye but may make her find B027 more natural.
Eriksson is professionally close to topological-materials and Hubbard-model physics and treats this as a possible bias toward B057 and B006, not a recusal matter.

Mehlig is in the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson but reports no collaboration with a credited person. Danielsson and Pearce report no specific conflict; Danielsson notes that Zoller appears in B060 and B006.
questions_for_round2: B027 versus B057: given six explicit supporters for B027 and two for B057, can the supporters of B057 say what evidence would move them, and can the supporters of B027 say what would move them?

Does the committee regard the lattice clock as a distinct invention from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes? If yes, which specific element should the citation name (magic-wavelength trapping, the 1e-18 level, many-body clock physics, tests of redshift)?
Should the B027 prize wait for the redefinition of the second, or does the committee judge that the science is mature without it? What would be lost by acting now and by waiting?
Can a Katori and Ye credit be defended against the claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Oates? Is Ye's role original invention or decisive development, and does the citation need to say which?

Can a Kane, Mele and Molenkamp credit for B057 be defended without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D contributors, or would a different configuration be required? Is the omission acceptable when Zhang is deceased?
What does B057 add to the 2016 topology prize, in terms the citation could state?

Should B053 (Olsson's and Pearce's first alternative) and B041 (Pearce's second alternative; Danielsson's first) be kept as serious alternatives to B027? If so, how would the Krivanek question (B053) and the credit within a large collaboration (B041) be resolved?
Does any member wish to propose a two-part configuration, for example B027 together with B057, and would the committee find the three-person limit workable for it?
summary.chair_observation: Support is concentrated in two entries: B027 has six explicit supporters and B057 two, and B027 is an alternative for two of them. Both turn on a question of attribution and a question of novelty relative to earlier prizes (2005 and 2012 for B027, 2016 for B057), and members are largely candid about both. Several members changed their first choice after reading the openings, so round 1 does not show how firm any position is. I have not counted any alternatives as support, and I take no position on the outcome.
